protected_invariants: the two offline CLIs (scripts/ops/stage_d_backup_snapshot.js and scripts/ops/stage_d_restore_verify.js) are byte-unchanged by this mission: live R2 wiring is added as two new entrypoints, never as a new flag on the offline CLIs, because 'the offline CLI cannot address a remote target' is a property proven and merged in PR #1911 and an endpoint flag on that CLI would destroy the property while leaving the file looking correct

OFFLINE_CLIS_UNCHANGED_NETLESS=YES: the offline CLIs continue to refuse every endpoint, bucket, region, credential and profile flag in both spellings, continue to link no SDK and to make no network request, and a regression test asserts both that they refuse the new live flag names and that neither file references the live loaders, the R2 transport or the SDK

there is no implicit credential discovery anywhere on the live path: no default location, no ~/.aws, no AWS_PROFILE, no AWS_* environment variable, no AWS_SHARED_CREDENTIALS_FILE, no instance metadata and no SDK provider chain; a load with no explicit path fails even when the SDK's own environment variables are set, and the property is additionally asserted structurally because 'this loader ignores the environment' is a claim about the code rather than about a list of variables

a secret value never reaches argv, stdout, stderr, a log, an error message, a report or an evidence file: the live CLIs refuse inline secret flags by name without echoing the value, both loaders name a rule rather than a value, both replace the JSON parser's own message because it quotes its input, the credential file's path is never reported, and credential errors are routed through a scrubber before anything is printed

the target identity is non-secret by construction and is not a credential channel: it is a closed nine-field schema whose values are additionally checked against credential value shapes, so a secret pasted into a field, or used as a JSON object key, is refused rather than accepted, ignored or echoed

no credential, API token or secret value is created, requested, read, printed, logged, copied or persisted by this mission, CREDENTIAL_CREATED=NO and CREDENTIAL_VALUE_INSPECTED=NO, and no credential value appears in the repository, the diff, a test fixture or an evidence file; every credential value in a test is synthetic and marked so that a leak would be detectable rather than merely asserted absent

the transport contract still admits exactly five verbs (putObjectCreateOnly, getObject, headObject, listObjects, describe) and still refuses all fourteen forbidden verbs including deleteObject, deleteObjects, deletePrefix, deleteGeneration, emptyBucket, removeObject, putObjectOverwrite, createBucket, deleteBucket, configureBucket, putBucketLock, putBucketLifecycle and putBucketPolicy; DELETE_CAPABILITY_EXPOSED=NO and no delete capability is required from the provider

create-only semantics are unchanged and are never emulated: the filesystem transport uses open(..., O_CREAT|O_EXCL) and the S3-compatible transport uses If-None-Match: '*', and a HEAD-then-PUT emulation is never used; only 412 and 409 are classified as a benign collision and every other failure stays a real failure

the configured prefix remains an addressing detail rather than part of a generation: the manifest records logical keys, the verifier compares the listed set against them for exact equality, listObjects strips the prefix on the way out and the provider is addressed in physical keys on the way in, and a test pins both halves because a leak would make a prefixed transport unable to verify a generation it had just written

bucket administration is out of scope and never performed: R2_BUCKET_CREATED=NO, R2_BUCKET_MODIFIED=NO, BUCKET_LOCK_CONFIGURED=NO and R2_BUCKET_LOCK_MODIFIED=NO, no Cloudflare REST API is called, and BUCKET_LOCK_CONFIGURATION=OUT_OF_SCOPE_FOR_THIS_MISSION; the runtime backup credential is required to be a DATA_PLANE_CREDENTIAL and must not possess bucket-administration authority, which is what makes NORMAL_BACKUP_RUNTIME_CAN_REMOVE_LOCK=NO true of it

the documentation does not overstate provider capability in either direction: the three-layer credential-scope model is recorded as current official documentation (long-lived token bucket-level scoping, temporary credential prefix and object scoping, and an explicit action list that is currently supported via local signing only) and the repository does not claim that R2 cannot prefix-scope credentials; an Indefinite Bucket Lock is not described as irreversible and the required terminology is used (INDEFINITE_RETENTION=YES, ADMINISTRATIVELY_REMOVABLE=YES, NORMAL_BACKUP_RUNTIME_CAN_REMOVE_LOCK=NO) with Bucket Lock described as a separate defensive layer

the live path is proven offline and only offline: every test runs with no network under a tripwire that seals http, https, net, tls, dns, dns.promises, http2, globalThis.fetch and globalThis.WebSocket, the seal covers child processes through a NODE_OPTIONS preload, and the r2 transport, the full generation harness and the live CLI preflight are all exercised against an in-memory stub SDK rather than against a provider

the live CLI preflight is classified OFFLINE_PREFLIGHT and reports live_connectivity_preflight: NOT_PERFORMED with network_calls_made: 0; it proves that the wiring loads, validates and constructs and does not claim to prove reachability, credential validity, permission sufficiency or the target's existence, and no live connectivity probe is performed by this mission

no production state is mutated: no production backup, production restore, production authority mutation, live fetch, DB write, raw write, training, prediction, backtest, model activation or migration apply is executed
Stage D is not started and no gate is advanced: BLOCKER_3 stays OPEN, GATE_2 stays NOT_ACCEPTED, GATE_3 stays NOT_AUTHORIZED and STAGE_D_STARTED=NO
